articles.title: SeaWolves ready to begin their fifth straight post season
articles.summary: Crowds filled the stands at UPMC Park as the Erie SeaWolves began another postseason. The Minor League Baseball team has reached a milestone, making the play...
articles.body:
Crowds filled the stands at UPMC Park as the Erie SeaWolves began another postseason.

The Minor League Baseball team has reached a milestone, making the playoffs for five straight years. It was a special night at UPMC Park, game one of the playoffs.

The SeaWolves are no stranger to their first-round opponents, the Richmond Flying Squirrels, but fans Tuesday night were hoping for a win for our home team.

"We had people here at nine am working hard and getting everything ready, from hospitality areas to on the field and the grounds crew working, so we're all getting our hours in and making sure UPMC Park is ready for this game one of the Southwest Division Series," said Laina Banic, the marketing director for the Erie SeaWolves.

The very last possible home game of the season is potentially Sunday if they win the Southwest Division. Then they would move on to play the Northeast winner.

articles.title: Kyle Schwarber, Colson Montgomery Have Chance To Break Not So Great MLB Record
articles.summary: Not all Major League Baseball Records are great to own
articles.body:
Colson Montgomery of the Chicago White Sox and Kyle Schwarber both have a chance to break the single-season strikeout record this year.

The record for strikeouts in a season by a batter is 223 strikeouts, set by Mark Reynolds in 2009. It's not a glamorous record to own, but it does not always mean a player had a terrible season. Over the years, many players have come close to beating Reynolds' record. Most recently, James Wood struck out 221 times last year, but had an .825 OPS and 31 home runs.

This year, Schwarber is at 210 strikeouts, and Montgomery is at 209. Montgomery struck out a bunch last year as well, but had a .840 OPS in 71 games. This year, his OPS is .712. However, he has been an important player for the Chicago White Sox, blasting 31 home runs in their unexpected season.

Schwarber has had the kind of season that makes teams completely forget about the strikeouts. He has a league-leading 44 home runs and an .869 OPS. Reynolds hit 44 home runs during his 2009 season.

Montgomery and the White Sox and Schwarber and the Phillies each have 12 games left this season. Both have a real chance to break Reynolds' record, but they have already put together great seasons. Their success, despite the strikeouts, is a glimpse into the modern offensive philosophy. Every team is chasing the long ball and is more willing to look past strikeouts.

articles.title: Carlos Correa Injury Update Reveals Astros Star's Status for Rest of MLB Season Amid Ankle Issue
articles.summary: The Houston Astros will be without their star shortstop for the remainder of the year.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros will be without their star shortstop for the remainder of the year.

Astros manager Joe Espada told reporters Tuesday that Carlos Correa will be out for the rest of the season amid an ankle issue that has sidelined him for most of the year.

Correa underwent surgery on his left ankle in May and faced a return timeline of six to eight months. He was initially set to miss the remainder of the season , but there was optimism as of late that he could make a return before the postseason.

The Athletic's Chandler Rome reported Tuesday that Correa planned to return to the team's spring training facility in Florida this week to meet with doctors and potentially receive clearance for a rehab assignment with Triple-A Sugar Land.

Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic noted last week that if Correa was able to return, the team was considering putting him at second base. He has only ever played at third base and shortstop in his career.

But the Astros' hopes of getting the three-time All-Star back on the field have seemingly now been squashed, and they'll have to continue their playoff push without him.

"The most important thing for him now is to focus on next season," Espada told reporters .

Espada said Correa did not suffer a setback in his recovery, but the rehab took a toll on his leg and ankle and created soreness.

In 32 games before his injury, Correa had hit three home runs and 16 RBI while slashing .279/.369/.418.

The Astros are currently sitting atop the AL West at 75-75, but they are just one game ahead of the second-place Texas Rangers. Houston will take on the Kansas City Royals starting Tuesday after being swept by the Tampa Bay Rays over the weekend.

articles.title: Astros manager Joe Espada confirms SS Carlos Correa will not return from ankle injury this season
articles.summary: Correa had been sidelined since May 4 due to a torn tendon in his ankle.
articles.body:
Houston Astros manager Joe Espada confirmed to reporters Tuesday that shortstop Carlos Correa will not return this season. Correa has been sidelined since the beginning of May due to an ankle injury. When the injury occurred, it was expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season.

In early August, however, Espada said Correa had been cleared to resume swinging a bat. The shortstop was expected to go out on a rehab assignment in the near future, with a chance to return before the postseason.

Espada said Tuesday that Correa has not suffered a setback or another injury that is preventing him from returning this year. Instead, the manager said the "daily workload" and the "recovery" became too much for the veteran shortstop.

Correa had been cleared for swinging and had begun taking ground balls at second base. Houston was trying to find a way to get him back into the lineup alongside Jeremy Peña at shortstop and Isaac Paredes at third, Correa's typical positions.

Correa initially tore a tendon in his ankle in a freak batting practice accident. Before the injury, he played in 32 games for Houston. The shortstop was slashing .279/.369/.418 with three home runs and 16 RBI.

The 31-year-old veteran is playing on a six-year, $200 million deal that he originally signed with the Minnesota Twins . Minnesota traded him back to Houston ahead of the 2025 trade deadline. The Astros have two more years of Correa on their books, and Houston has four club options between 2029 and 2032.

Correa has a history of ankle injuries. He had two free-agent megadeals with the San Francisco Giants and the New York Mets fall through due to concerns about his ankle's health. Those were about his right ankle, though; this torn tendon is in the shortstop's left ankle.

As of Tuesday, Houston has a 75-75 record and a one-game lead over the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Correa will now turn his attention to getting fully healthy for the 2027 season.

articles.title: Rare Mickey Mantle Photo from 1951 Sells for $3M, More Than Doubles Record
articles.summary: A rare photo of New York Yankees legend Mickey Mantle sold for a historic price on Tuesday.
articles.body:
A rare photo of New York Yankees legend Mickey Mantle sold for a historic price on Tuesday.

Per The Athletic's Larry Holder , a photo of the Hall of Famer from 1951 sold for a record-breaking price of $3 million in a private sale brokered by Hunt Auctions.

The unsigned photo of Mantle was used for his iconic 1952 Topps baseball card and is PSA Type I authenticated. The sale shattered the record for an autographed sports photo, which was previously held by a Shoeless Joe Jackson signed image sold by Christie's and Hunt Auctions in 2021 for $1.47 million.

Holder noted that a PSA Type I photo is "a first generation photograph, developed from the original negative, during the period (within approximately two years of when the picture was taken)."

Hunt Auctions said that the photo sold of Mantle was initially used by the International News Service in a local news release and was not used for national distribution.

"The demand for high-end original Type I photographs from new collectors and investors coming into the space is at an all-time high," said PSA photo authenticator Henry Yee, per Holder. "The supply however for this material is extremely scarce. When an item of this caliber is offered for sale, often it is sold privately and does not even make it to public auction — such as in this case."

Mantle was a 20-time All-Star and three-time MVP who won seven World Series with the New York Yankees during his 18-year career. He retired in 1968 and died in 1995.

articles.title: MLB World Series favorite faces serious trouble as the regular season enters its final few weeks of the year
articles.summary: Dodgers’ three-peat hopes threatened by Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and Andy Pages injuries as Edwin Diaz struggles entering 2026 season’s final stretch.
articles.body: Somehow, there are just two weeks remaining in the 2026 Major League Baseball regular season. Once again, this baseball season has shown how and why trying to predict it remains one of the most futile endeavors in sports. And that lack of predictability is even more apparent as several postseason races look set to come down to the last few games of the season. The American League playoff race has several spots up for grabs, with teams hoping to avoid the wrong kind of history: becoming the first sub-.500 team to reach the postseason in a full season. While the Chicago White Sox have led the American League Central for most of the season, the Cleveland Guardians are just 1.5 games back with two games remaining in their series on Tuesday and Wednesday. WITH ONE MONTH LEFT, AMERICAN LEAGUE TEAMS ARE HEADING TOWARDS AN EMBARRASSING, HISTORIC LOW In the AL West, the Houston Astros are clinging to a one-game lead over the Texas Rangers at 75-75, though the teams don't play each other the rest of the year. Then there's the wild card race. The Guardians currently sit in the third wild card position at 76-75, but the Toronto Blue Jays, left for dead months ago, have clawed their way back into it, just one game back. If the Rangers can’t catch the Astros, they’re still just 1.5 games back of the third wild-card spot. Even the 73-78 Baltimore Orioles are only three games behind Cleveland. Somehow. So there are two teams competing for the AL Central, two teams competing for the AL West and four competing for the final wild card spot behind the Yankees and Red Sox. Those division races will also determine which team gets a first-round bye and who's forced into a best-of-three wild card series. Cleveland, Chicago, Houston and Texas are all within just a few games of each other, meaning that the second and third seed might not be determined until the final weekend. Hilariously, there are just five teams with a positive run differential in the AL, and one of them, the Tigers, is 71-79 and effectively eliminated. On the NL side, there are just two teams fighting for the final wild card spot, the Arizona Diamondbacks and San Diego Padres. While the Padres have become baseball's hottest team, Arizona's still just 2.5 games behind. More importantly, those two teams play each other in the final series with the season tiebreaker up for grabs, meaning that the race may not be clinched until literally the last day of the year. Last game, two division rivals potentially playing for a postseason berth at Petco Park. A dream scenario for the league. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Speaking of the west, while the Dodgers have clinched a postseason berth, they're still battling with the Braves to clinch the second seed behind the runaway Milwaukee Brewers. And that bye might be even more important than it normally is, because the Dodgers are in trouble. Serious trouble. While they've accumulated a tremendous amount of talent between their player development, fortuitous trades and their obviously large financial advantages, much of it is far from full strength heading into October. And it might cost them a chance at a three-peat. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Shohei Ohtani is on the injured list for the first time as a Dodger, after dealing with knee and arm injuries for most of the season. Not only will he not be available to pitch in the playoffs, he won't be eligible to return until the final weekend of the season. Freddie Freeman has been battling right knee soreness severe enough to keep him out of the lineup several times over the past week. Andy Pages, who's been one of the Dodgers most valuable players this season, fractured his hand on a hit by pitch several weeks ago and, while he's started taking swings, has no set return date before the postseason. Then there's Edwin Díaz. Díaz, who signed for $69 million in the offseason, went from a 1.63 ERA in 2025 to 11.85 in 2026. He went down for several months with an arm injury himself, only to return and look... worse. One of the most expensive relief pitchers in baseball has seven saves and four blown saves, allowing a remarkable 37 baserunners and 18 runs in 13.2 innings. He's back on the injured list, and just gave up five runs in a rehab appearance in the minor leagues. Edgardo Henriquez, who's helped fill in for Díaz at the back end of the bullpen, has been outstanding over the last month. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Except he's now hurt too, going on the injured list with back issues that will keep him out for the remainder of the regular season. Roki Sasaki too, had gone on the IL and was expected back this past weekend, only for manager Dave Roberts to say Tuesday that he won't return until next week at the earliest. It's a testament to the Dodgers' depth that they're still a very good team, even with all these problems, and the promotion of top prospect Josue De Paula has already paid off. But these are very real and significant injury issues to key players, and the timeline to get them all back is compressed, to say the least. Securing a first-round bye would give them a few extra days’ rest before starting the NLDS, but Ohtani, Pages, Diaz, Freeman, Henriquez and Sasaki may either not play again during the regular season or make only a few at-bats or a single appearance before the playoffs. They’ve also turned Brice Turang, Andrew Vaughn and Jake Bauers into elite offensive contributors. With the Dodgers taking on water and big-name players like Mookie Betts, Will Smith, Freddie Freeman and Kyle Tucker well below their career averages, might this be the Brewers’ year? When they say you can't predict baseball, this is why.
